<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% ------------------------------------------------------------------
% Cells are exactly the coordinates that appear in the input
cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% Grid size – the highest row and column indices that occur
max_row(MR) :- MR = #max{R : input(R,_,_)}.
max_col(MC) :- MC = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% 4‑connected neighbour offsets
delta(0,1).
delta(0,-1).
delta(1,0).
delta(-1,0).

% Adjacent cells – used for the flood‑fill
adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R = Rp + DR,
    C = Cp + DC,
    cell(R,C),
    input(R,C,V),
    V != 3.

% Boundary cells – cells on the outer rim that are not colour 3
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = MR.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = MC.

% Flood‑fill from the boundary through cells that are not colour 3
outside(R,C) :- boundary(R,C).
outside(R,C) :- outside(Rp,Cp), adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C),
                input(R,C,V), V != 3.

% Cells that are not reachable from the boundary and are not colour 3
interior(R,C) :- cell(R,C), not outside(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3.

% Allowed output colours for each cell
allowed(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,3).                                   % colour 3 stays 3
allowed(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 3, outside(R,C).             % reachable cells keep their colour (V ≠ 3)
allowed(R,C,4) :- interior(R,C), input(R,C,0).                  % interior zero cells become 4
allowed(R,C,V) :- interior(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != 3.   % interior non‑zero cells keep colour

% Exactly one colour for each cell, chosen from the allowed set
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(0..9), allowed(R,C,Col) } 1 :- cell(R,C).

% Dimensions of the input grid
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Block row index (floor(R/N))
br(R,BR) :- 0 =< BR, BR =< N-1, BR * N =< R, R =< (BR+1) * N.

% Block column index (floor(C/M))
bc(C,BC) :- 0 =< BC, BC =< M-1, BC * M =< C, C =< (BC+1) * M.

% The cell (R,C) is covered by the block with origin (BR,BC)
block(R,C,BR,BC) :- br(R,BR), bc(C,BC).

% Relative coordinates inside the block
dr(R,BR,DR) :- R = BR * N + DR.
dc(C,BC,DC) :- C = BC * M + DC.

% Exactly one block covers each output cell
output_cell(R,C) :- block(R,C,BR,BC).

% If the origin cell of the block is zero, the whole block is zero
output(R,C,0) :- input(BR,BC,0), block(R,C,BR,BC).

% If the origin cell is non‑zero, copy the original input into the block
output(R,C,V_sub) :- input(BR,BC,V_origin), V_origin != 0,
                      block(R,C,BR,BC), dr(R,BR,DR), dc(C,BC,DC), input(DR,DC,V_sub).

% Exactly one output colour for each cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).
</asp>

The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). % Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)

   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,

outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% neighbor offsets (4‑connected)
neighbor(0,1).
neighbor(0,-1).
neighbor(1,0).
neighbor(-1,0).

% adjacent cells (4‑connected)
adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C) :-
    neighbor(DR,DC),
    R = Rp + DR,
    C = Cp + DC,
    input(R,C,_).

% boundary cells (outer rim, not colour 3)
boundary(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, R > 0, not input(R+1, C, _).
boundary(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, C > 0, not input(R, C+1, _).

% cells reachable from the boundary without crossing colour 3
outside(R,C) :-
    boundary(R,C).
outside(R,C) :-
    outside(Rp,Cp), adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3.

% interior cells (not reachable and not colour 3)
interior(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, not outside(R,C).

% allowed colours per cell
% 3 stays 3
allowed(R,C,3) :- input(R,C,3).

% outside cells keep their colour (colour ≠ 3)
allowed(R,C,Col) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3, outside(R,C), Col = V.

% interior zero cells become 4
allowed(R,C,4) :- interior(R,C), input(R,C,0).

% interior non‑zero, non‑3 cells keep their colour
allowed(R,C,Col) :-
    interior(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != 3, Col = V.

% domain of output (same cells as input)
cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% exactly one colour for each cell, chosen among allowed colours
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(0..9), allowed(R,C,Col) } 1 :- cell(R,C).

<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). </transformation>

% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>

% Define cell existence
cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% Grid dimensions
max_row(MR) :- MR = #max{R : input(R,_,_)}.
max_col(MC) :- MC = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.

delta(0,1).
delta(0,-1).
delta(1,0).
delta(-1,0).

% Adjacent cells (used for flood‑fill)
adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C) :-
    delta(DR,DC),
    R = Rp+DR,
    C = Cp+DC,
    cell(R,C),
    input(R,C,V),
    V != 3.

% Boundary cells: cells on the outer rim that are not colour 3
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = MR.
boundary(R,C) :- cell(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = MC.

% Flood‑fill from the boundary through cells that are not colour 3
outside(R,C) :- boundary(R,C).
outside(R,C) :- outside(Rp,Cp), adjacent(Rp,Cp,R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3.

% Cells that are not reachable from the boundary and are not colour 3
interior(R,C) :- cell(R,C), not outside(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 3.

% Exactly one colour for each cell, chosen from the allowed set
1 { output(R,C,Col) : color(0..9), allowed(R,C,Col) } 1 :- cell(R,C).
